pageCache.pageTitle: New Hinksey Primary School – 'Living life in its fullness'
pageCache.text:
A Message of Welcome
Discover New Hinksey CE Primary – a vibrant, nurturing school where curiosity is celebrated, individuality is valued, and children grow into confident, happy learners.
Our ‘village school’ is a unique haven in the heart of a throbbing city where we blend the charm of a close-knit community with the diverse opportunities that urban life offers.
Our team of excellent teachers and support staff are dedicated to nurturing every child’s potential. They bring passion, creativity, and expertise into the classroom, and they foster curiosity and a love of learning.
We offer a wide-ranging curriculum that includes art and music for all, ensuring that every child has the chance to explore their creative talents. We are proud of our diverse community supporting children from various backgrounds, including those who are disadvantaged, have English as an additional language, or have special educational needs.
At New Hinksey we want our children to thrive in body, heart and spirit, in alignment with our school’s vision, that is inspired by the words of Jesus:
“I have come that you may have life in all its fullness” (John 10:10)
Helen Nash
About New Hinksey…
“New Hinksey CE Primary School is such a fantastic place. It really stands out for its nurturing environment and commitment to multicultural education founded on Christian principles, housed in inspiring historic buildings. The staff are very experienced, with a perfect mix of specialisms, and they create a warm, supportive, personalised atmosphere where kids thrive both academically and personally.”
“Pupils are proud of their diverse school community. The school’s vision for pupils to live ‘life in all its fullness’ is truly felt by all. Pupils are happy and positive about their school where they know that they are valued for their individuality. They have strong relationships with the school staff who help them if they have any worries. Parents and carers value the nurturing and caring atmosphere of the school.”
“This is a school at the heart of its community. Pupils and adults feel cherished so that they have high aspirations for themselves now and in the future.”
“New Hinksey is a school where everyone does indeed feel special and encouraged to succeed. This is because the staff know the children really well and believe everyone is worthy of their time and effort.”

pageCache.pageTitle: Breakfast & After School Club – New Hinksey Primary School
pageCache.text:
Breakfast & After School Club
Morning Club
New Hinksey runs a Morning Club from 7.45am to 8.40am. There is a daily charge of £5 which includes breakfast. Breakfast includes a selection of juice, cereal, toast, croissants, crumpets, waffles or fruit. The children have a calm start to the day, playing games, watching tv, drawing as well as being fed. They are taken to their classes for the start of the day.
After School Club
We also have an After School Club which runs from 3.10pm to 6pm. There is a daily charge of £12.50 per session. After School Club is staffed by enthusiastic staff who wish to make sure that the children have the best time possible while keeping them safe. The children have time outside to play daily (unless it is too wet in which case they use the hall). They have a snack time and then it is time for other activities. These can be creative, imaginative or just playing games. There are opportunities for cooking, going to the park and enjoying multi sports.
The children in both clubs have the opportunity to mix with children from other classes and it is wonderful to see these relationships develop. There is no organised homework or reading time – the purpose of the club is to have fun.
Places can be booked by emailing Claire on admin.3213@new-hinksey.oxon.sch.uk. We ask for 48 hours notice for booking places. Payment is made through Arbor. We also accept many different types of Childcare Vouchers.

Music
At New Hinksey Primary School:
• Music is taught weekly throughout the year by a subject specialist and is fully inclusive
• Pupils develop the key musical skills of listening, performing and singing and learn about music from a broad range of genres and traditions
• Pupils experience whole-class ensemble teaching programmes. Individual instrumental lessons are offered and are accessible and affordable for all pupils including the most disadvantaged and children with SEND
• Singing is celebrated and high-quality singing is embedded into the life of the school, with pupils and staff regularly singing together in music lessons and singing assemblies

Procedures for Child Absence
Unplanned Absences
We understand that not all absences are planned and some may be beyond individual control. When these situations arise parents must contact the school as soon as possible on any day their child is unable to attend school. This can be done by calling the school on 01865 242169 or emailing: admin.3213@new-hinksey.oxon.sch.uk. If phoning the school please be aware that the office is unmanned between 8.30am and 9.00am whilst staff do gate duty and see the children into classes from the playground. If the child is unwell, the school may ask about the type of illness, as the school needs to be informed about possible contagious infections that may spread to others in the school.
Please click here for advice about whether your child might be too ill to attend school/nursery.
Medical Appointments
We would expect appointments to take place outside school hours, but, if necessary, children can be taken out to leave school for short periods for medical or dental appointments. Please make sure you have informed school staff about these appointments and report to the school office on arrival to be let in to collect your child. The school may request more information about such absences.
Request for Absences
Children need to be in school for all sessions, so that they can make the most progress possible. If a parent feels that there is a circumstance necessitating a request for leave of absence for a child to attend, e.g. a very special event, then we expect parents and carers to contact school at soon as possible in advance and to put in writing the reasons for requesting absence. We strongly recommend parents and carers to take their family holiday in the normal school holiday periods, so no learning is disrupted.
As of August 2024, no term-time holidays will be authorised and are likely to incur a penalty charge from Oxfordshire County Council – please click here to see our attendance policy.
Extended Leave of Absence
We would ask for all leaves of absence to be put in writing. A doctor’s note may be requested should your child be absent for a long period of time. Should a pupil be on an extended leave for a long period of time they may be taken off roll and have to re-apply for a place at the school when they wish to return.
